purpose: libpng is a PNG image read/write library using zlib compression.

functions.png_get_uint_16: Converts 2 big-endian bytes in `buf` to a `png_uint_16`. Use it to read 16-bit values from PNG data. It always returns the combined value; no error checking or byte-order handling beyond big-endian.
functions.png_malloc_default: `png_malloc_default` is libpng’s fallback allocator: it ignores any app memory hook and uses the library’s base malloc. Use it only with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr==NULL` it returns `NULL`. On allocation failure it calls `png_error(png_ptr,"Out of Memory")` instead of returning `NULL`.
functions.png_write_end: `png_write_end` finishes PNG output after at least one IDAT has been written. Call it with `png_ptr` and optional `info_ptr` to emit remaining chunks (e.g. tIME/text). If no IDATs were written, it errors; NULL `png_ptr` returns immediately.
functions.png_get_uint_31: `png_get_uint_31` reads a 32-bit big-endian value from `buf` and validates it fits in PNG’s 31-bit unsigned range. Use it when decoding PNG fields that must be ≤ `PNG_UINT_31_MAX`. If out of range, it calls `png_error` and aborts via libpng’s error handling.
functions.png_get_compression_buffer_size: Returns the current compression buffer size for the png struct. Use with a valid `png_ptr`; if NULL, it returns 0. On read structs it returns `IDAT_read_size` (or `PNG_IDAT_READ_SIZE`), otherwise on write structs it returns `zbuffer_size`.
functions.png_set_invert_alpha: `png_set_invert_alpha` enables the `PNG_INVERT_ALPHA` transform in `png_ptr`. Call it before reading/processing image data to invert alpha values. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_strip_alpha: `png_set_strip_alpha` enables libpng’s read-transform to drop the alpha channel. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading image data. If read transforms are no longer allowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_STRIP_ALPHA`.
functions.png_process_data_pause: `png_process_data_pause` is a push-mode helper to stop `png_process_data` and report how many input bytes must be resent. Use only inside `png_process_data`. `save!=0` saves pending data and returns 0; otherwise it returns unsaved remaining bytes, excluding libpng-cached data.
functions.png_destroy_read_struct: Destroys a read-side PNG context and frees associated `png_info`/`end_info` structs. Call it when finished reading; pass pointers to the structs. If `png_ptr_ptr` is NULL or `*png_ptr_ptr` is NULL, it returns. It also nulls `*png_ptr_ptr` after cleanup.
functions.png_get_y_offset_microns: Returns the stored y offset in micrometers from the oFFs chunk. Use it only when `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are non-NULL and `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid. If the offset unit isn’t micrometers, or oFFs isn’t present/supported, it returns 0.
functions.png_set_background: `png_set_background` configures read-time alpha/tRNS compositing: transparent pixels are blended against a chosen background color. Use it after reading the PNG header; pass the background color, gamma mode, and whether expansion is needed. Behavior depends on gamma code and file state.
functions.png_get_io_ptr: Returns the user-supplied I/O pointer set on `png_ptr`. Use it to retrieve your custom read/write context inside callbacks. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns `png_ptr->io_ptr`.
functions.png_write_chunk_end: `png_write_chunk_end` finishes a chunk begun by `png_write_chunk_start()`: it writes the 4-byte CRC in one I/O operation. Use it after writing the chunk data. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_unknown_chunk_location: Sets the `location` for an entry in `info_ptr->unknown_chunks`. Use it only for a valid chunk index after unknown chunks are stored. Invalid location bits trigger `png_app_error`; then libpng coerces to a fallback location.
functions.png_set_read_user_transform_fn: Sets the read-side user transform callback. Call it to register `read_user_transform_fn`; libpng marks `PNG_USER_TRANSFORM` and stores the pointer. If read-user-transform support is disabled, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_mem_ptr: `png_get_mem_ptr` returns the user-supplied `mem_ptr` stored in `png_ptr`, or `NULL` if `png_ptr` is `NULL`. Use it to retrieve the pointer associated with libpng’s custom memory functions.
functions.png_get_interlace_type: `png_get_interlace_type` returns the image’s interlace type from `info_ptr`. Call it with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; otherwise it returns `0`. It just reads metadata and does no processing.
functions.png_write_png: `png_write_png` is a convenience high-level write helper: it writes the PNG header/info, then applies requested write transforms and outputs image data. Use it only with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and when `info_ptr` has IDAT rows; otherwise it returns or errors.
functions.png_create_write_struct_2: Creates a write-side `png_struct` with custom error/warn handlers and custom alloc/free hooks. Use it before any write setup. On success it initializes zlib defaults; on failure it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_set_sCAL: `png_set_sCAL` stores the PNG sCAL pixel-size chunk. Use it with positive `width`/`height`; invalid values are ignored with a warning. It converts doubles to ASCII then calls `png_set_sCAL_s` to save the unit and dimensions.
functions.png_get_chunk_malloc_max: `png_get_chunk_malloc_max` returns the current per-chunk malloc limit from `png_ptr->user_chunk_malloc_max`. Use it to query the limit set on a PNG read/write struct. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_benign_errors: Sets how `png_benign_error()` is handled. Call with `allowed!=0` to downgrade benign/app warnings/errors to warnings; `0` restores default error behavior. It just flips flags in `png_ptr`.
functions.png_save_int_32: `png_save_int_32` stores a signed 32-bit value into a 4-byte PNG buffer by casting to `png_uint_32` and calling `png_save_uint_32`. Use it when writing 32-bit integers to PNG-formatted bytes. It performs no range checks or sign handling beyond the cast.
functions.png_set_pCAL: `png_set_pCAL` stores a pCAL chunk in `info_ptr`: calibration purpose, X0/X1, equation type, units, and params. Call it with non-NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr/purpose/units` and valid `type` (0–3) and `nparams` (0–255). Invalid args/error cases return early.
functions.png_get_pixels_per_meter: Returns square-image resolution from `pHYs` only. Use with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; it returns `x_pixels_per_unit` when `PNG_INFO_pHYs` is set, units are meters, and X==Y. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_get_x_offset_pixels: Returns the x offset from the oFFs chunk, but only when `info_ptr` is valid and the unit is pixels. Use after reading PNG info. If `oFFs` is missing, unsupported, or not pixel-based, it returns `0`.
functions.png_chunk_benign_error: Reports a “benign” chunk problem. Use during chunk processing with `png_ptr` and a message. If `PNG_FLAG_BENIGN_ERRORS_WARN` is set, it emits a warning; otherwise it calls `png_chunk_error` and treats it as fatal.
functions.png_longjmp: `png_longjmp` is libpng’s safe wrapper for `longjmp(png_ptr->jmpbuf, val)`. Use it in apps instead of calling `longjmp` directly. If `longjmp_fn` and `jmp_buf_ptr` are set, it jumps there; otherwise it calls `PNG_ABORT()` and terminates.
functions.png_set_crc_action: `png_set_crc_action` sets libpng’s CRC-error policy for critical and ancillary chunks. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading. Critical CRCs can be kept with warning/quiet, or error/quit; discard is invalid for critical data.
functions.png_get_bKGD: `png_get_bKGD` retrieves the image’s stored background color from `info_ptr` if `PNG_INFO_bKGD` is set. Pass valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `background`; on success it stores a pointer to `info_ptr->background` and returns `PNG_INFO_bKGD`, else 0.
functions.png_set_sRGB: Sets the image to the sRGB colorspace and records the rendering intent. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` before writing info. If either is NULL, it returns immediately; otherwise it updates `info_ptr->colorspace` and syncs the info.
functions.png_get_IHDR: `png_get_IHDR` retrieves IHDR header fields from `info_ptr` into caller-supplied pointers. Use it after valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` exist; any output arg may be NULL to skip. Returns 0 if either pointer is NULL, otherwise fills width/height/bit depth/color/interlace/compression/filter.
functions.png_read_info: `png_read_info` reads the PNG signature and all header/info chunks up to image data (e.g., IHDR, PLTE, etc.). Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` before reading pixels. It returns early on NULL; errors occur if chunk order is invalid, e.g., IDAT before IHDR.
functions.png_get_header_version: Returns libpng’s compile-time header version string, plus date/newline (and “NO READ SUPPORT” if built without read support). `png_ptr` is unused; pass any valid pointer or ignore it. It just returns a constant string.
functions.png_info_init_3: `png_info_init_3` is a deprecated compatibility helper to initialize a `png_info` struct, possibly reallocating it if the caller’s struct is too small. Use it only for old code; modern libpng should use the current init/allocation APIs. If size is insufficient, it frees the old block, allocates a new one, stores it back, then zeroes the struct.
functions.png_set_write_fn: `png_set_write_fn` sets libpng’s custom output callbacks and user `io_ptr`. Use it to replace default file I/O with your own write/flush functions. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns. `write_data_fn` may fall back to defaults when stdio is enabled; flush may be ignored if flush support is off.
functions.png_set_gAMA_fixed: Sets the image file gamma in `info_ptr->colorspace`. Use it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is NULL, it returns immediately. It then updates colorspace gamma and syncs `info_ptr` metadata.
functions.png_set_compression_mem_level: Sets zlib’s memory level for PNG compression. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing/compression. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing; otherwise it stores `mem_level` in `png_ptr->zlib_mem_level`.
functions.png_get_pCAL: `png_get_pCAL` retrieves the pCAL chunk fields from `info_ptr`. Use it after reading info, with all output pointers non-NULL. It returns `PNG_INFO_pCAL` and fills purpose/X0/X1/type/nparams/units/params; otherwise returns 0 if missing/invalid args or pCAL not present.
functions.png_image_write_to_stdio: Writes a `png_image` to a `FILE*` stream. Use only with a valid `image` version, non-NULL `file` and `buffer`; it initializes writing, sets stdio IO, then writes via `png_safe_execute` and frees the image. Returns success/failure.
functions.png_set_longjmp_fn: `png_set_longjmp_fn` sets/returns libpng’s `jmp_buf` and the `longjmp` function to use for error handling. Call it once per `png_ptr` before use; if `jmp_buf_size` fits, it uses встроенный buffer, else allocates one and may return `NULL` on alloc/ABI mismatch.
functions.png_set_unknown_chunks: `png_set_unknown_chunks` stores caller-supplied unknown chunk records in `info_ptr` for later read/write handling. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and a non-NULL array. It returns immediately on bad args; if unknown-chunk support is disabled, it reports an error for the affected read/write mode.
functions.png_get_x_offset_microns: Returns the image X offset in micrometers from `info_ptr` when `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid and `offset_unit_type == PNG_OFFSET_MICROMETER`. Use after reading metadata; otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_sig_cmp: `png_sig_cmp` checks whether bytes in `sig` match the PNG 8-byte signature. Use it on a buffer of file header bytes; it returns 0 on match, nonzero on mismatch. `num_to_check==0` or `start>7` fails; it also clamps `num_to_check` to 8.
functions.png_write_rows: `png_write_rows` is a convenience wrapper to write multiple image rows. Pass a `png_structp`, an array of row pointers, and `num_rows`; it calls `png_write_row` for each row in order. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_cHRM_XYZ_fixed: Sets the cHRM chunk from fixed-point XYZ primaries. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; NULL returns immediately. It stores endpoints, validates via `png_colorspace_set_endpoints`, marks `PNG_COLORSPACE_FROM_cHRM` on success, then syncs `info_ptr`.
functions.png_write_chunk: `png_write_chunk` is a thin wrapper to write a PNG chunk: it converts the 4-byte chunk name string to a chunk ID, then calls `png_write_complete_chunk` to write size, type, optional data, and CRC. Use it when emitting a chunk during PNG writing.
functions.png_set_sCAL_s: `png_set_sCAL_s` stores the sCAL chunk in `info_ptr` using string width/height. Use it only with non-NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr`, unit 1 or 2, and valid nonnegative numeric strings. Invalid unit/strings trigger `png_error`; NULL pointers return immediately.
functions.png_set_pHYs: `png_set_pHYs` stores pHYs metadata in `info_ptr`: X/Y pixels-per-unit and unit type, then marks `PNG_INFO_pHYs` valid. Use it when preparing image info for writing. If `png_ptr` or `info_ptr` is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_alpha_mode: `png_set_alpha_mode` is a convenience wrapper that sets alpha handling plus output gamma. Use it on `png_ptr` with a mode and screen/output gamma; it just forwards to the fixed-point version. Behavior depends on `mode` and `output_gamma` (e.g. sRGB, linear, Mac 1.8).
functions.png_set_swap: `png_set_swap` enables byte-swapping for 16-bit PNG data. Call it on a valid `png_ptr`; it only sets `PNG_SWAP_BYTES` when `bit_depth == 16`. If `png_ptr` is NULL or depth isn’t 16, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_cHRM_fixed: `png_set_cHRM_fixed` sets PNG cHRM chromaticity values in `info_ptr` from fixed-point xy coords. Use it before writing; if `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL it returns. On success it marks colorspace as from cHRM and syncs info.
functions.png_set_add_alpha: Adds an alpha byte to gray/RGB images by calling `png_set_filler`. Use it before reading/transforming image data, with a filler value and location flag. If filler isn’t applied, no alpha transform is enabled.
functions.png_set_tRNS_to_alpha: `png_set_tRNS_to_alpha` enables expansion of a PNG `tRNS` transparency chunk into an alpha channel. Call it on `png_ptr` before reading image data. If `png_rtran_ok` fails, it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_EXPAND | PNG_EXPAND_tRNS`.
functions.png_set_background_fixed: `png_set_background_fixed` configures read-time alpha composition against a supplied background color. Use it before decoding. It enables `PNG_COMPOSE|PNG_STRIP_ALPHA`, clears alpha encoding/optimize flags, stores background/gamma, and sets/clears `PNG_BACKGROUND_EXPAND`. If gamma is UNKNOWN, it warns and returns.
functions.png_get_int_32: Converts 4 PNG bytes to signed `png_int_32`. Used to read possibly negative PNG values safely. Returns the value if it fits; on invalid/overflow cases it returns `0` as a safe fallback.
functions.png_write_flush: `png_write_flush` forces a sync flush of pending PNG IDAT output. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` during writing; if `png_ptr` is NULL or all rows are already written, it does nothing. It then flushes the output buffer.
functions.png_get_error_ptr: Returns the user-supplied error callback pointer from `png_ptr`. Use it after `png_create_*`/error setup to retrieve your context. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns `png_ptr->error_ptr`.
functions.png_set_compression_buffer_size: Sets the zlib/IDAT buffer size for a png struct. Call it before compression/reading uses the buffer. `size==0` or `>PNG_UINT_31_MAX` is an error; if a write buffer is already in use, it warns and does nothing.
functions.png_set_text: `png_set_text` adds text chunks to `info_ptr` for writing. Call it with `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, a text array, and count. It delegates to `png_set_text_2`; if that reports failure, it raises `png_error` for insufficient memory.
functions.png_convert_to_rfc1123_buffer: Builds an RFC1123 date string into a 29-byte buffer for PNG text/HTTP headers. Use with valid `png_time`; returns 1 on success, 0 if `out==NULL` or fields are out of RFC1123 range.
functions.png_write_info_before_PLTE: Design aim: start PNG output by writing the signature and IHDR, i.e. all info that must come before PLTE. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; NULL returns immediately. It’s idempotent via `PNG_WROTE_INFO_BEFORE_PLTE`, so repeated calls won’t rewrite.
functions.png_get_x_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image’s X resolution in pixels/inch, derived from `png_get_x_pixels_per_meter()`. Use it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` after reading metadata. If no X resolution is set, it returns the converted result of that underlying value.
functions.png_create_write_struct: Creates and initializes a `png_struct` for PNG writing. Call it first before write setup; pass libpng version, error context, and error/warn callbacks. If user memory support is off, it uses default allocators; otherwise it delegates to `png_create_write_struct_2`.
functions.png_write_image: `png_write_image` writes a full image row-by-row using `png_write_row`. Use it after PNG write setup, passing `image` as an array of row pointers. If interlacing is enabled, it writes all passes; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_text: Returns text metadata from `info_ptr`. Use after reading a PNG; pass valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. If text exists, it stores `info_ptr->text` and count in outputs and returns the count. Otherwise returns 0 and sets `*num_text` to 0 if given.
functions.png_handle_as_unknown: `png_handle_as_unknown` checks `chunk_name` against `png_ptr->chunk_list` and returns that chunk’s stored `keep`/handling flag. Use it to decide whether a chunk needs special handling; NULL/empty list or no match => default handling (`PNG_HANDLE_CHUNK_AS_DEFAULT`).
functions.png_get_user_transform_ptr: Returns the user-supplied pointer for custom transform callbacks. Use it after setting user transforms to retrieve your context/state. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns `png_ptr->user_transform_ptr`.
functions.png_create_read_struct_2: Creates a read-side `png_struct` with custom error/warn handlers and custom alloc/free hooks. Use it before reading PNG data. On success it marks the struct as read mode, sets IDAT read size, and enables benign/app warning flags; on failure it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_set_filter: `png_set_filter` sets libpng’s row-filtering policy for **writing**. Use `method=0` (`PNG_FILTER_TYPE_BASE`) and pass allowed filter bits in `filters`. It maps to `png_ptr->do_filter`; invalid method/filter combos can trigger an error, and NULL `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_image_write_to_file: Writes a `png_image` to a named file. Use with a valid `image` version, non-NULL `file_name` and `buffer`; it opens `"wb"` then delegates to `png_image_write_to_stdio`. Returns 1 on success, 0 on invalid args/open/write/flush/fclose failure.
functions.png_set_scale_16: `png_set_scale_16` enables libpng’s 16-bit→8-bit scaling transform. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading rows. If required read transforms aren’t OK (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_SCALE_16_TO_8`.
functions.png_get_cHRM_fixed: `png_get_cHRM_fixed` reads stored cHRM chromaticity endpoints from `info_ptr` into fixed-point outputs. Pass non-NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr`; any output ptr may be NULL to skip. Returns `PNG_INFO_cHRM` if endpoints exist, else 0.
functions.png_save_uint_32: `png_save_uint_32` stores a 32-bit unsigned value into `buf` in big-endian/network byte order. Use it when writing PNG chunk/data fields. It always writes 4 bytes; `buf` must point to at least 4 writable bytes.
functions.png_chunk_error: `png_chunk_error` reports a fatal libpng error with the current chunk name prepended. Use it only when `png_ptr` is valid; otherwise it falls back to `png_error(png_ptr, error_message)`. It never returns (`PNG_NORETURN`).
functions.png_get_iCCP: Retrieves an image’s iCCP chunk data from `info_ptr`. Use after reading PNG info; pass non-NULL `name`, `profile`, `proflen` (and optional `compression_type`). Returns `PNG_INFO_iCCP` only if valid; otherwise 0. Compression type is reported as base since profile is already uncompressed.
functions.png_get_signature: Returns the PNG signature bytes stored in `info_ptr`. Use it only after a valid PNG header has been read and both `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are non-NULL. If either is NULL, it returns NULL.
functions.png_get_tRNS: `png_get_tRNS` retrieves tRNS transparency info from `info_ptr`. Use after reading PNG info; pass output pointers you want filled. For palette images it returns `trans_alpha` and `trans_color`; for non-palette, mainly `trans_color`. Returns flags if tRNS is present, else 0.
functions.png_get_sCAL_fixed: `png_get_sCAL_fixed` reads an sCAL chunk from `info_ptr`, returning unit, width, and height as `png_fixed_point`. It only succeeds if `PNG_INFO_sCAL` is valid; otherwise returns 0. Uses floating-point parsing internally, so needs FP support.
functions.png_set_tRNS: `png_set_tRNS` stores tRNS transparency info into `png_info`/`png_struct` for later write/read processing. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if `trans_alpha` is non-NULL it frees old tRNS data, allocates/copies palette alpha (when `num_trans` is in range), and handles color-key transparency via `trans_color`.
functions.png_set_gray_to_rgb: `png_set_gray_to_rgb` enables grayscale→RGB expansion. Call it on a `png_struct` before reading/conversion. It first ensures transforms are allowed; if not, it does nothing. Otherwise it expands 1/2/4-bit gray to 8-bit, then marks `PNG_GRAY_TO_RGB`.
functions.png_set_option: Sets a libpng runtime option on `png_ptr`. Call with a valid `png_structrp`, an even `option` in range, and `onoff` nonzero/zero. It updates `png_ptr->options` and returns the previous 2-bit setting; invalid args return `PNG_OPTION_INVALID`.
functions.png_get_header_ver: `png_get_header_ver` returns the libpng header version string used to build the library. It ignores `png_ptr`, so any valid pointer is acceptable. Use it to compare build-time header version with the library version; it always returns `PNG_LIBPNG_VER_STRING`.
functions.png_get_x_offset_inches: Returns the X offset in inches from the stored micron value. Use it after reading valid `info_ptr`; it just converts microns to inches in float, so no extra checks beyond normal libpng validity.
functions.png_get_user_chunk_ptr: Returns the user-supplied `user_chunk_ptr` stored in `png_ptr`. Use it to retrieve the per-application pointer for custom chunk handling. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_malloc_warn: `png_malloc_warn` allocates `size` bytes via libpng’s allocator. Use it with a valid `png_ptr`; on success it returns the pointer. If allocation fails, it emits `png_warning(png_ptr, "Out of memory")` and returns `NULL`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it just returns `NULL`.
functions.png_get_y_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image’s Y resolution in pixels/inch, converting from the stored pixels/meter value. Use it with a valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` after reading metadata. If no Y ppu is set, it returns the converted value from the underlying meter field.
functions.png_set_flush: `png_set_flush` sets the row interval for output flushes. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before writing; `nrows<=0` disables flushing, negative values are treated as 0, and `NULL` is ignored.
functions.png_set_gamma_fixed: Sets gamma correction for reading: `screen_gamma` is display gamma, `file_gamma` overrides the file’s gamma. Use before row processing. If transforms aren’t allowed, it returns. In libpng 1.6+, nonpositive values are errors.
functions.png_get_x_offset_inches_fixed: Returns the image’s X offset in inches as a fixed-point value. Use it to read metadata from `info_ptr`; it converts the stored X offset from microns to inches. If the offset isn’t present, it follows the underlying `png_get_x_offset_microns` behavior.
functions.png_get_y_offset_inches_fixed: Returns the Y offset as a fixed-point value in inches. Use it to read the image’s vertical offset from `info_ptr`; it converts the stored micron offset via `png_fixed_inches_from_microns`. If the offset isn’t present, it follows the underlying `png_get_y_offset_microns` behavior.
functions.png_get_filter_type: Returns the image’s stored filter_type from `info_ptr`. Use it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is NULL, it returns 0. It’s a simple getter, not a setter or validator.
functions.png_get_sCAL: `png_get_sCAL` retrieves the sCAL chunk from `info_ptr`: it returns `PNG_INFO_sCAL` and fills `unit`, `width`, `height` from stored strings via `atof()`. Use only when `info_ptr` is valid and sCAL is present; otherwise it returns 0 and leaves outputs unchanged.
functions.png_set_bgr: `png_set_bgr` enables the `PNG_BGR` transform, telling libpng to treat pixel bytes as BGR instead of RGB. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading/writing image data. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_progressive_ptr: Returns the user I/O pointer set for progressive (push) read callbacks. Use it with a valid `png_ptr` to retrieve your app context. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns `png_ptr->io_ptr`.
functions.png_get_pHYs_dpi: `png_get_pHYs_dpi` retrieves the PNG pHYs chunk values: X/Y pixels per unit and unit type. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; it returns `PNG_INFO_pHYs` if the chunk exists and any requested outputs are filled. If `pHYs` is absent or args are NULL, it returns 0.
functions.png_get_tIME: `png_get_tIME` retrieves the image’s `tIME` chunk. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `mod_time`; on success it stores a pointer to `info_ptr->mod_time` and returns `PNG_INFO_tIME`. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_set_read_fn: Replaces libpng’s default input with a user callback. Call it after creating `png_ptr`, pass your context in `io_ptr`, and a `read_data_fn` (or NULL to restore default if stdio is enabled). If write fn was set too, it clears it and warns.
functions.png_get_compression_type: Returns the stored PNG compression type from `info_ptr`. Use it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It does not compute or validate the value.
functions.png_get_rows: `png_get_rows` returns `info_ptr->row_pointers`, i.e. the scanline pointer array produced by `png_read_png()`. Use it only after reading with `png_read_png()`. If `png_ptr` or `info_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0` (NULL).
functions.png_get_gAMA_fixed: `png_get_gAMA_fixed` retrieves the image’s stored gAMA chunk as a fixed-point gamma value. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output pointer; on success it writes `info_ptr->colorspace.gamma` and returns `PNG_INFO_gAMA`, else returns 0.
functions.png_set_cHRM_XYZ: `png_set_cHRM_XYZ` sets PNG cHRM chromaticity primaries using XYZ tristimulus values. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` before writing the image; it converts doubles to fixed and forwards to `png_set_cHRM_XYZ_fixed`.
functions.png_set_error_fn: Sets custom error/warning callbacks and user data on `png_ptr`. Call it after creating `png_struct` and before PNG I/O. If `png_ptr` is NULL it does nothing; if warnings aren’t supported, `warning_fn` is ignored.
functions.png_set_user_transform_info: Sets user-transform context for libpng callbacks: stores `user_transform_ptr`, depth, and channel count. Call before read-image init/update; if called after `png_start_read_image`/`png_read_update_info` in a read struct, it errors and returns. Null `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_get_gAMA: `png_get_gAMA` retrieves the image’s gAMA chunk value. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `file_gamma`; on success it stores gamma in `*file_gamma` and returns `PNG_INFO_gAMA`. If args are null or gamma isn’t present, it returns 0.
functions.png_save_uint_16: `png_save_uint_16` writes a 16-bit unsigned integer to `buf` in PNG/network byte order (big-endian). Use it to store values 0–65535 into a 2-byte buffer. It always writes two bytes; higher bits are discarded.
functions.png_write_row: `png_write_row` writes one image row during PNG encoding. Call it after `png_write_info()`, then once per row in order. On first row it checks header state/transforms; if `png_ptr` is NULL it returns, and missing `png_write_info()` causes an error.
functions.png_get_oFFs: `png_get_oFFs` retrieves the image offset metadata from `info_ptr` (x/y offset + unit type). Use it only when `info_ptr` has `PNG_INFO_oFFs` and all output pointers are non-NULL. On success it fills outputs and returns `PNG_INFO_oFFs`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_set_packing: `png_set_packing` enables packing expansion for images with bit depth < 8, so pixels are handled as 1 byte each. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before row processing. If `bit_depth >= 8` or `png_ptr==NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_PLTE: Returns the image’s PLTE chunk data. Call with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL `palette`; `num_palette` is filled with entry count. If `PNG_INFO_PLTE` isn’t set or args are invalid, it returns 0 and leaves outputs unchanged.
functions.png_set_invalid: `png_set_invalid` clears selected bits in `info_ptr->valid`. It’s meant to mark metadata/chunks as no longer valid, especially after your app frees a chunk that `png_free_data()` didn’t free. Use only with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it just masks off `mask`.
functions.png_set_bKGD: `png_set_bKGD` stores a suggested background color in `info_ptr` and marks `PNG_INFO_bKGD` valid. Use it after reading/creating a `png_struct`/`png_info` and pass a non-NULL `png_color_16`. If any arg is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_calloc: `png_calloc` is a libpng helper to allocate `size` bytes and zero-initialize them. Use it like `malloc` via `png_ptr`; it returns `NULL` on allocation failure, otherwise a cleared block.
functions.png_set_write_user_transform_fn: Sets a write-side user transform callback. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; it marks `PNG_USER_TRANSFORM` and stores the function pointer. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. Passing `NULL` callback just clears/sets no callback.
functions.png_set_gamma: `png_set_gamma` sets the screen and file gamma values for gamma correction. Call it before reading the PNG header for best results; if called after, it overrides the file’s gamma info. `file_gamma` is the inverse of screen gamma.
functions.png_get_rowbytes: `png_get_rowbytes` returns `info_ptr->rowbytes`, i.e. the bytes needed for one transformed row. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_shift: `png_set_shift` enables the PNG_SHIFT transform and stores the “true” bit depths for channels. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` and `png_color_8` info. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_alpha_mode_fixed: Design: set alpha handling + gamma for output, often for premultiplied-alpha composition. Use after read init, pass a valid screen/output gamma (fixed-point). It validates range and errors if out of expected bounds; if unsupported/read state bad, it returns early.
functions.png_image_write_to_memory: Writes an `png_image` to a memory buffer, or just counts required bytes if `memory==NULL`. Use only with valid `image`/version, `buffer`, and `memory_bytes`; `memory==NULL` sets `*memory_bytes=0` for easier error checking.
functions.png_get_y_offset_pixels: Returns the image Y offset in pixels from the oFFs chunk. Call with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it returns `y_offset` only if `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is set and unit type is `PNG_OFFSET_PIXEL`, otherwise 0.
functions.png_set_iCCP: `png_set_iCCP` stores an ICC color profile in `info_ptr` for writing. Use it with a non-NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr/name/profile` and `PNG_COMPRESSION_TYPE_BASE`; invalid compression errors. It validates the profile first and skips copying if the profile is bad/inconsistent.
functions.png_warning: `png_warning` reports a non-fatal libpng warning. Pass a valid `png_ptr` and message; if `warning_fn` is set, it calls that, otherwise the default handler. It may strip leading `#... ` error numbers/text before reporting.
functions.png_get_current_row_number: Returns the current row being processed, mainly for use inside a user transform callback. For interlaced images it’s the sub-image row for the current pass, resetting each pass. If `png_ptr` is NULL, returns `PNG_UINT_32_MAX`.
functions.png_init_io: `png_init_io` sets `png_ptr->io_ptr` to a `FILE*` so libpng’s default I/O can use that stream. Call it after creating `png_ptr` and before read/write ops. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately; it doesn’t open/close the file.
functions.png_read_image: `png_read_image` is for reading the entire image into a caller-provided row-pointer array. Call it after setup/update info; for interlaced PNGs, enable interlace handling first. It returns immediately on `png_ptr==NULL`; if interlace handling is missing, it warns and may auto-fix.
functions.png_convert_to_rfc1123: Deprecated helper to format a `png_time` as RFC1123 text. Call with a valid `png_structrp` and `ptime`; on success it returns `png_ptr->time_buffer`. If `ptime` is invalid, it warns and returns `NULL`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_write_chunk_start: `png_write_chunk_start` begins writing a PNG chunk by emitting its length and 4-byte chunk name. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`, chunk name string, and data length; it simply forwards to `png_write_chunk_header`.
functions.png_get_uint_32: `png_get_uint_32` converts 4 bytes in `buf` from PNG/network big-endian order to a host `png_uint_32`. Use it on a 4-byte buffer. It always returns the assembled 32-bit value; no error checks or side effects.
functions.png_set_IHDR: `png_set_IHDR` stores the PNG IHDR fields in `info_ptr` and validates them. Use it when creating/writing a PNG header. If `png_ptr` or `info_ptr` is NULL, it returns. It sets width/height/depth/type/methods, then checks them and derives channels from `color_type`.
functions.png_read_rows: `png_read_rows` is a convenience API to read multiple image rows in sequence. Pass arrays of row pointers; if `display_row` is non-NULL, each row gets a matching display buffer. If `png_ptr` is NULL it returns immediately. If `row` is NULL, no rows are read.
functions.png_create_read_struct: Creates/initializes a `png_struct` for reading. Call it first with libpng version, error context, error/warn callbacks; it returns a read handle or NULL on failure. If user memory support is enabled, it forwards to `png_create_read_struct_2`.
functions.png_convert_from_struct_tm: Converts a C `struct tm` into libpng `png_time` fields. Use it by passing a valid `png_time*` and `struct tm*`; it copies year/month/day/hour/min/sec with month adjusted to 1–12. No validation or range checks are done.
functions.png_get_valid: `png_get_valid` checks whether a given chunk flag is set in `info_ptr->valid`. Use it with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it returns `valid & flag` if both are present, else 0. It does not modify anything.
functions.png_set_check_for_invalid_index: Sets whether libpng checks for invalid palette indices. Call with `allowed > 0` to disable the check (`num_palette_max = 0`), otherwise enable it (`-1`). It only updates this internal flag.
functions.png_get_current_pass_number: Returns the current interlace pass index from a valid `png_ptr`. Use it after creating/reading a PNG to query progress in Adam7 decoding. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `8` as an invalid sentinel.
functions.png_set_text_compression_strategy: Sets the zlib compression strategy used for text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing text; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It simply stores the given `strategy` in `png_ptr->zlib_text_strategy`.
functions.png_convert_from_time_t: Converts a `time_t` to libpng `png_time` using `gmtime()`. Pass a valid `png_timep` and `time_t`; it fills `ptime` from UTC time. If `gmtime()` fails, behavior depends on `png_convert_from_struct_tm` receiving a null `tm*`.
functions.png_set_write_status_fn: Sets the callback used during PNG writing to report row-write status. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. Passing `NULL` as `write_row_fn` clears/disables the callback.
functions.png_get_copyright: Returns libpng’s copyright/version text. `png_ptr` is unused and may be NULL. Use it only to query/display the built-in string; it always returns a constant string, with content fixed by `PNG_STRING_COPYRIGHT` or the compiled-in fallback.
functions.png_destroy_write_struct: Destroys write-side libpng state. Call with `png_structpp` and optional `png_infopp` after finishing or on error. It frees the `png_info` via `png_destroy_info_struct`, then the `png_struct`, and sets `*png_ptr_ptr` to `NULL` if non-NULL.
functions.png_error: `png_error` is libpng’s fatal-error reporter: it may strip `#nnnn` codes/text per flags, then reports the message and does not return. Use it only for unrecoverable PNG errors; pass a valid `png_ptr` when possible, and expect it to abort via libpng’s error handling/jump mechanism.
functions.png_get_chunk_cache_max: Returns the current user-set maximum number of chunks PNG will cache. Use it to query `png_ptr`’s `user_chunk_cache_max`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_eXIf_1: Stores eXIf chunk data in `info_ptr`. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and a buffer of `num_exif` bytes; it frees any previous `info_ptr->exif`, allocates new storage, and warns/returns on OOM. Null `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` => no-op.
functions.png_set_expand_gray_1_2_4_to_8: Sets the read-transform to expand 1/2/4-bit grayscale images to 8-bit. Call it before reading rows. If transforms are disabled (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_EXPAND`.
functions.png_set_text_compression_level: Sets the zlib compression level used for non-IDAT text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is NULL it does nothing. It just stores `level` in `zlib_text_level` for later text compression.
functions.png_get_cHRM_XYZ: `png_get_cHRM_XYZ` retrieves cHRM chromaticity endpoints in XYZ form from `info_ptr`. Call it after reading metadata; pass output pointers or NULL to ignore fields. It returns nonzero only if `png_ptr/info_ptr` are valid and endpoints exist; otherwise no values are written.
functions.png_set_compression_level: `png_set_compression_level` sets the zlib compression level in `png_ptr` for later PNG writing. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before compression/write operations. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing; otherwise it stores `level` directly.
functions.png_set_user_limits: Sets per-reader max image width/height. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before `png_set_IHDR()`. Images exceeding either limit are rejected; `0x7fffffff` for both accepts any PNG size. `NULL` `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_destroy_info_struct: `png_destroy_info_struct` frees all memory in a `png_info` object. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr_ptr`; if `*info_ptr_ptr` is non-NULL, it nulls that pointer first, frees internal data, zeros the struct, then frees it. If `png_ptr` or `info_ptr_ptr` is NULL, or `*info_ptr_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_text_compression_window_bits: Sets the zlib window size for text compression. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before writing text. Values are clamped to 8..15; out-of-range inputs trigger a warning and are adjusted. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_write_info: `png_write_info` writes the PNG header/info chunks to the output stream. Call it after filling `png_struct`/`png_info`, before writing image data. It writes PLTE/tRNS/etc as needed; for palette images, a valid palette is required, else it errors.
functions.png_set_compression_window_bits: Sets PNG zlib compression window size for writing. Use on a valid `png_ptr` before compression; values are clamped to 8..15, with warnings if outside. `NULL` does nothing. It only stores the chosen window bits.
functions.png_set_mem_fn: Replaces libpng’s default alloc/free with user callbacks. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before allocations; `mem_ptr` is passed to your functions. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_data_freer: `png_data_freer` changes `info_ptr->free_me` bits to assign who frees selected `png_info` data. Use it only with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and a mask; `PNG_DESTROY_WILL_FREE_DATA` sets bits, `PNG_USER_WILL_FREE_DATA` clears them. Invalid `freer` triggers `png_error`; NULL args return.
functions.png_process_data: `png_process_data` feeds available input to libpng’s push/streaming decoder. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it stores the buffer, then repeatedly processes data until the internal buffer is empty. If either pointer is `NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_pHYs: `png_get_pHYs` retrieves the PNG pHYs chunk: pixel density and unit type. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; outputs are filled only for non-NULL pointers. It returns `PNG_INFO_pHYs` if the chunk is present and any requested field was set, else 0.
functions.png_permit_mng_features: Sets which MNG features libpng may accept. Call with a valid `png_ptr`; it masks `mng_features` to `PNG_ALL_MNG_FEATURES`, stores it, and returns the permitted bits. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0` and does nothing.
functions.png_set_eXIf: `png_set_eXIf` is a deprecated stub. It does nothing except issue a warning: “png_set_eXIf does not work; use png_set_eXIf_1”. Use `png_set_eXIf_1` instead; `info_ptr` and `exif` are ignored.
functions.png_set_filter_heuristics: `png_set_filter_heuristics` was meant to configure libpng’s row-filter selection heuristics for writing PNGs (weighted vs unweighted). In this source it’s deprecated and a no-op: all args are ignored. Use `png_set_filter_heuristics_fixed` only if supported.
functions.png_set_expand: `png_set_expand` enables libpng’s expand transforms: palette→RGB, low-bit-depth→8-bit, and tRNS transparency→alpha when present. Call it before reading image data. If transforms are already locked out, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_expand_16: `png_set_expand_16()` enables read-time expansion to 16-bit channels. Use it before `png_read_*` to force palette→RGB and expand any tRNS transparency. If transforms aren’t allowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing.
functions.png_get_user_width_max: Returns the current user-set max image width from `png_ptr`. Use it to query the limit previously configured in the PNG read/write struct. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_build_grayscale_palette: Builds a grayscale palette for indexed PNGs. Call with `bit_depth` 1, 2, 4, or 8 and a valid `png_colorp`; it fills palette entries with evenly spaced gray values. If `palette == NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_read_user_chunk_fn: Registers a read-time callback for unknown chunks. Use it to inspect/save/handle chunks; return <0 on error, 0 to let libpng save it, >0 to tell libpng to discard it. It just stores the function and user pointer.
functions.png_set_oFFs: `png_set_oFFs` stores the image offset metadata (x/y and unit type) in `info_ptr` and marks `PNG_INFO_oFFs` valid. Use it only when `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are non-NULL; otherwise it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_palette_to_rgb: `png_set_palette_to_rgb` requests libpng to expand paletted images to RGB and, if present, expand tRNS transparency too. Call it before reading image data. If transforms are disallowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing.
functions.png_write_sig: Writes the 8-byte PNG file signature to the output stream. Call it during PNG encoding, after setting `sig_bytes` if some bytes were already written. It writes only the remaining bytes, updates I/O state, and sets `PNG_HAVE_PNG_SIGNATURE` when `sig_bytes < 3`.
functions.png_set_strip_16: `png_set_strip_16` enables the 16-to-8-bit transform. Call it before reading image data to discard the low byte of 16-bit samples. If transformations aren’t allowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing.
functions.png_get_user_height_max: Returns the user-set maximum image height from `png_ptr->user_height_max`. Use it to query the current limit; pass a valid `png_ptr`. If `png_ptr` is null, it returns 0.
functions.png_get_io_state: `png_get_io_state` is a simple getter for libpng’s current I/O state flags. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` to inspect what libpng is doing during read/write I/O. It returns `png_ptr->io_state` directly; it doesn’t modify state or perform checks.
functions.png_free_default: `png_free_default` is libpng’s default deallocator. Use it to free memory previously allocated by libpng’s default allocator. If `png_ptr` or `ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately; otherwise it calls `free(ptr)`. Deprecated.
functions.png_set_compression_strategy: Sets the zlib compression strategy for a PNG write. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before compression starts. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns. It also marks the strategy as custom, disabling libpng’s automatic strategy selection.
functions.png_get_hIST: `png_get_hIST` retrieves the image histogram chunk from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL `hist`. If `PNG_INFO_hIST` is present, it stores the histogram pointer and returns `PNG_INFO_hIST`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_set_tIME: `png_set_tIME` stores a valid PNG `tIME` chunk value in `info_ptr` for later writing. Call it before the `tIME` chunk is written; NULL args or repeat use after `PNG_WROTE_tIME` are ignored. Invalid date/time fields trigger a warning and are not stored.
functions.png_set_filler: `png_set_filler` adds a filler/alpha byte to 8/16-bit Gray or RGB images. On read, it’s always valid and only affects read transforms; on write, it configures output channel layout. If unsupported on read, libpng errors.
functions.png_set_text_compression_method: Sets the text-chunk compression method in `png_ptr`. Use it before writing text; if `png_ptr` is NULL it returns. Any method other than 8 triggers a warning, but the value is still stored in `zlib_text_method`.
functions.png_set_progressive_read_fn: Sets up libpng’s progressive/push-decoding callbacks. Call once before feeding data: provide user context plus `info_fn`, `row_fn`, `end_fn`. If `png_ptr` is NULL it does nothing; otherwise it stores the callbacks and installs push input via `png_set_read_fn`.
functions.png_get_unknown_chunks: Returns the count of unknown chunks in `info_ptr` and stores the chunk array via `*unknowns`. Use it after reading/setting info. If any arg is NULL, it returns 0 and does not set `*unknowns`.
functions.png_get_io_chunk_type: `png_get_io_chunk_type` returns the 4-byte PNG chunk type currently being processed (`png_ptr->chunk_name`). Use it only with a valid `png_ptr` during I/O callbacks or chunk handling. It has no side effects and just reports the current chunk name.
functions.png_get_pixel_aspect_ratio: Returns the pixel aspect ratio from a valid pHYs chunk as `y_pixels_per_unit / x_pixels_per_unit`. Call with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if pHYs is absent or `x_pixels_per_unit==0`, it returns `0.0`.
functions.png_get_image_height: Returns the image height from `info_ptr`. Use it after you have valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`. If either is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_color_type: Returns the image’s stored `color_type` from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It’s a simple getter, not a validator.
functions.png_reset_zstream: `png_reset_zstream` resets libpng’s zlib inflate stream. Use it only with a valid `png_structrp`; `NULL` returns `Z_STREAM_ERROR`. It calls `inflateReset()` and warns that window bits are reset to the maximum. Deprecated.
functions.png_free: `png_free` releases memory previously allocated by `png_malloc()`. Call it with the same `png_ptr`; if either `png_ptr` or `ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately. If a user free callback is set, that is used; otherwise the default free is used.
functions.png_process_data_skip: `png_process_data_skip` is a deprecated/unused helper for streaming input: call it only outside `png_process_data()`. It should tell the app how many input bytes to skip, but in current libpng it’s not implemented, warns, and always returns 0.
functions.png_set_chunk_cache_max: `png_set_chunk_cache_max` sets `png_ptr->user_chunk_cache_max` if `png_ptr` is non-NULL. It’s used to configure the maximum chunk cache limit for a PNG read struct. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_start_read_image: Starts row-reading setup for an image. Call once before reading rows, typically after any update/transforms. If `png_ptr` is NULL it does nothing. If called twice after init, it reports a duplicate-call error.
functions.png_set_sPLT: `png_set_sPLT` adds one or more sPLT palette entries to `info_ptr` for writing. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, non-NULL `entries`, and `nentries > 0`. If args are bad it returns; if growth fails, it reports “too many sPLT chunks” and returns.
functions.png_get_bit_depth: `png_get_bit_depth` returns the image bit depth from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It’s a simple accessor, not a setter or validator.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_file: Design: open a file and start initializing a `png_image` for reading PNG data. Use: pass a valid `png_image` with matching `version` and a non-NULL filename. Behavior: opens file in `"rb"`, sets ownership, then reads header. Returns error if args invalid, file open fails, or init/header read fails.
functions.png_set_cHRM: `png_set_cHRM` sets PNG chromaticity (white/red/green/blue xy) in `info_ptr`. Use it before writing the image; it converts doubles to fixed and delegates to `png_set_cHRM_fixed`. Invalid/out-of-range values are handled by the fixed conversion/error path.
functions.png_read_row: `png_read_row` reads one decoded row from a PNG stream. Call it after `png_read_info`/setup; it initializes row state if needed, handles interlace pass info, and fills `row` (and optional `display_row`). If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_quantize: `png_set_quantize` enables palette quantization (`PNG_QUANTIZE`) to reduce an image to `maximum_colors`. Use it before read/transform processing. If `full_quantize==0`, it builds a direct index map; if `num_palette>maximum_colors` and `histogram` is given, least-used colors are discarded.
functions.png_get_sPLT: `png_get_sPLT` retrieves the `sPLT` chunk list from `info_ptr`. Pass valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output pointer `spalettes`; it stores the palette array there and returns the number of palettes. If any arg is NULL, it returns 0.
functions.png_progressive_combine_row: Merges the library’s internally buffered progressive-interlace row into `old_row` for display. Call only from the progressive row callback; `new_row` is just a non-NULL flag (typically `row_buf+1`). If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns; if `new_row` is NULL, nothing is combined.
functions.png_create_info_struct: Allocates and zero-initializes a `png_info` struct for a given `png_ptr`. Use it after `png_create_read_struct`/`png_create_write_struct`, often before setting error handlers. Returns `NULL` if `png_ptr` is `NULL` or allocation fails; it does not raise errors.
functions.png_malloc: `png_malloc` allocates `size` bytes using libpng’s allocator tied to `png_ptr`. Use it only with a valid `png_ptr`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; if allocation fails, it calls `png_error(png_ptr, "Out of memory")` and does not return normally.
functions.png_get_x_pixels_per_meter: Returns the PNG pHYs X resolution in pixels/meter. Use after reading info, with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; it returns `x_pixels_per_unit` only if `PNG_INFO_pHYs` is set and unit is meter, otherwise 0.
functions.png_set_packswap: `png_set_packswap` requests packing-order swap for sub-8-bit pixels. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading/converting. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_PACKSWAP` only when `bit_depth < 8`.
functions.png_read_end: `png_read_end` finishes reading a PNG stream after image data. Call it after `png_read_image`/row reads to consume any pending IDAT data and read the trailing chunks. If `png_ptr` is NULL it returns; it may also report benign errors like invalid palette index.
functions.png_set_rgb_to_gray: Sets RGB→gray conversion coefficients. Call before reading rows; it forwards to `png_set_rgb_to_gray_fixed` after converting doubles to fixed-point. `error_action` controls what happens if the coefficients are invalid, and status can be queried with `png_get_rgb_to_gray_status`.
functions.png_set_keep_unknown_chunks: Sets the default policy for unknown chunks, and optionally a chunk-name list. Use with `keep` to choose handling mode; `num_chunks==0` only sets the default. Invalid `keep` errors. Negative `num_chunks` means ignore all unknown and most known chunks.
functions.png_get_sBIT: `png_get_sBIT` retrieves the image’s stored significant-bit info from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `sig_bit`; on success it sets `*sig_bit` to `info_ptr->sig_bit` and returns `PNG_INFO_sBIT`. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_get_eXIf_1: Retrieves eXIf metadata from `info_ptr`. Call after reading info; if `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, `exif` are non-NULL and `PNG_INFO_eXIf` is valid, it returns that flag and fills `num_exif`/`exif`. Otherwise returns 0 and leaves outputs unchanged.
functions.png_set_swap_alpha: `png_set_swap_alpha` enables the `PNG_SWAP_ALPHA` transform in `png_ptr`. Use it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading/writing to swap alpha channel position during conversion. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_access_version_number: `png_access_version_number()` returns the libpng version used to build the library (`PNG_LIBPNG_VER`). Call it with no args to query the library’s compile-time version; it just returns that 32-bit number, with no side effects.
functions.png_set_text_compression_mem_level: Sets the zlib memory level used when compressing text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. Otherwise it simply stores `mem_level` in `png_ptr->zlib_text_mem_level`.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_memory: Initializes a `png_image` to read PNG data from a memory buffer. Use with a valid `image`, matching `PNG_IMAGE_VERSION`, non-NULL `memory`, and `size>0`. On success it sets memory I/O and reads the PNG header; otherwise it returns an error.
functions.png_get_cHRM: `png_get_cHRM` retrieves the image’s chromaticity endpoints from `info_ptr` (from cHRM, or also iCCP/sRGB-derived data). Call after reading info; pass output pointers you want filled. Returns 0 if no endpoints are present, otherwise the chunk is reported via the returned mask.
functions.png_get_sRGB: Returns sRGB info from `info_ptr`. Use after reading metadata; pass non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `file_srgb_intent`. If `PNG_INFO_sRGB` is set, it stores the rendering intent and returns `PNG_INFO_sRGB`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_read_update_info: Updates read-side info after transforms are set, so row setup matches the final output format. Call it once before reading rows. If `png_ptr` is NULL it does nothing; if called twice after row init, it reports a duplicate-call error.
functions.png_set_sCAL_fixed: Sets the sCAL chunk from fixed-point width/height. Use only with positive values; invalid width/height are ignored with a warning. It converts both to ASCII then calls `png_set_sCAL_s` to store the physical pixel size/unit.
functions.png_free_data: Frees libpng-owned data in `info_ptr` per `mask`/`num`. Use with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; `num==-1` frees all items of that type, otherwise only the indexed item. If ptrs are NULL, it returns.
functions.png_image_free: `png_image_free` releases resources owned by a `png_image`. Call it when done with the image. It only frees if `image`, `image->opaque` are non-NULL and no error context is active (`error_buf==NULL`); otherwise it does nothing here.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_stdio: Begins PNG image reading from a `FILE*` stream. Use with a valid `png_image` (`version==PNG_IMAGE_VERSION`) and non-NULL `file`; it initializes read state, sets `io_ptr`, then reads the header. Returns 0 on invalid args/init failure, else success/failure from header read.
functions.png_set_compression_method: `png_set_compression_method` sets the PNG zlib compression method in `png_ptr`. Use it before writing/encoding. PNG only supports method 8; other values just trigger a warning, but the value is still stored. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_gAMA: Sets the PNG gAMA chunk in `info_ptr` using a double gamma value. It’s just a wrapper that converts `file_gamma` to fixed-point and calls `png_set_gAMA_fixed`; behavior depends on that conversion/validation.
functions.png_get_y_offset_inches: Returns the image Y offset in inches from the stored micron value. Use with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; it converts directly to float to avoid overflow. If the offset isn’t set, it follows `png_get_y_offset_microns()` behavior.
functions.png_set_read_status_fn: Sets a callback for row-read status updates during PNG decoding. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; passing `NULL` does nothing. It simply stores the function pointer, and a `NULL` callback disables the status hook.
functions.png_set_PLTE: `png_set_PLTE` stores the image palette in `info_ptr`. Use it before writing the PNG, with `num_palette` entries in `palette`. For palette images, length must be ≤ `1<<bit_depth`; otherwise ≤ `PNG_MAX_PALETTE_LENGTH`. Invalid length errors for palette images, warns/returns for others.
functions.png_get_rgb_to_gray_status: Returns the current RGB-to-gray conversion status stored in `png_ptr`. Use it after libpng has performed or evaluated rgb-to-gray handling. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_sBIT: `png_set_sBIT` stores the image’s significant-bit info in `info_ptr` and marks `PNG_INFO_sBIT` valid. Call it with non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `sig_bit`; otherwise it does nothing. It simply copies `*sig_bit` into `info_ptr->sig_bit`.
functions.png_get_y_pixels_per_meter: Returns the Y resolution from pHYs in pixels/meter. Use with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` after reading info. If pHYs is absent, unsupported, or unit isn’t meters, it returns 0.
functions.png_chunk_warning: `png_chunk_warning` reports a non-fatal libpng warning for a specific chunk, prepending the chunk name to the message. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` and warning text; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it forwards directly to `png_warning`.
functions.png_get_pixel_aspect_ratio_fixed: Returns the pixel aspect ratio as fixed-point y/x from pHYs. Use only with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; it returns 0 if pHYs is absent/invalid or on overflow.
functions.png_get_pixels_per_inch: Returns image resolution in pixels/inch, derived from the stored pixels/meter value. Use it after reading/setting PNG info with a valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`. If no pHYs/resolution is present, it returns 0.
functions.png_read_png: `png_read_png()` is a convenience one-shot reader: it calls `png_read_info()` then applies requested transforms and reads the image. Use it only after setting up read structs and any needed transforms. If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL it returns; oversized height errors out.
functions.png_get_libpng_ver: Returns the libpng version string for the library build. Use it to query the version from an existing `png_ptr`; it simply calls `png_get_header_ver(png_ptr)` and returns that result.
functions.png_set_hIST: `png_set_hIST` stores a PNG `hIST` chunk in `info_ptr`. Use it only after `info_ptr->num_palette` is valid (1..PNG_MAX_PALETTE_LENGTH) and pass a histogram array. If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL or palette size is invalid, it returns with a warning; otherwise it frees old hIST data and allocates new storage.
functions.png_set_sRGB_gAMA_and_cHRM: Sets the image colorspace to sRGB and marks gAMA/cHRM for writing too. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if either is NULL it returns. If sRGB setup fails, nothing is marked, then info is synced.
functions.png_set_rows: `png_set_rows` assigns the scanline pointer array used by `png_write_png()`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if `row_pointers` is non-NULL, it marks `PNG_INFO_IDAT` valid. If replacing an existing different array, old rows are freed. If either struct is NULL, it returns.
functions.png_get_channels: `png_get_channels` returns the number of color channels in the image from `info_ptr->channels`. Use it after valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are available. If either is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_image_width: `png_get_image_width` returns the image width in pixels from `info_ptr`. Call it only with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_sCAL_s: Returns sCAL metadata from `info_ptr`. Call after reading info; if `png_ptr/info_ptr` are non-NULL and `PNG_INFO_sCAL` is set, it fills `unit`, `width`, `height` and returns `PNG_INFO_sCAL`. Otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_benign_error: `png_benign_error` reports a recoverable libpng problem. If `PNG_FLAG_BENIGN_ERRORS_WARN` is set, it issues a warning; otherwise it calls the fatal error path. In read mode with a current chunk, it uses chunk-specific warning/error handlers.
functions.png_set_rgb_to_gray_fixed: Sets up RGB→grayscale conversion with fixed-point weights. Call it before reading image data, after IHDR is known. `error_action` controls behavior on non-grayable pixels: none/warn/error. It only applies when the transform is allowed; palette images are rejected.
functions.png_write_chunk_data: Writes the data bytes for a chunk begun by `png_write_chunk_start()`, while updating the CRC. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; if `data==NULL` or `length==0`, it does nothing. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_cHRM_XYZ_fixed: Returns cHRM chromaticity endpoints in fixed-point XYZ. Use after `png_read_info`/`png_set_cHRM_XYZ_fixed`; pass output pointers or NULL to ignore. If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL or endpoints absent, it returns 0 and writes nothing.
functions.png_set_interlace_handling: Enables libpng to handle interlaced PNGs during reading. Call it before `png_read_update_info` or `png_start_read_image`; it returns 7 for interlaced images, 1 otherwise. You still must read each row/rows for every pass.
functions.png_image_finish_read: `png_image_finish_read` completes a `png_image_begin_read` decode into user buffer. It validates `image`/version, checks `row_stride` for overflow, uses default stride if 0, and may apply `background`/`colormap`. Fails safely on bad args or size issues.
functions.png_set_invert_mono: `png_set_invert_mono` enables the `PNG_INVERT_MONO` transform on a `png_struct`. Call it before reading/processing a 1-bit monochrome image to swap black/white interpretation. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_palette_max: Returns the maximum palette size from `png_ptr->num_palette_max`. Use only with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; otherwise it returns `-1`. It’s a simple query helper, not a setter or validator.
functions.png_set_chunk_malloc_max: Sets libpng’s per-chunk malloc limit. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading chunks to cap memory used for a single user chunk. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_filter_heuristics_fixed: A no-op stub in this build. It’s meant to set PNG filter-selection heuristics (weighted/unweighted, weights/costs) for writing, but here all args are ignored and it has no effect.
functions.png_get_eXIf: `png_get_eXIf` is a stub/compatibility API. It warns that it “does not work” and tells you to use `png_get_eXIf_1` instead. It ignores `info_ptr`/`exif` and always returns 0, so it should not be used for reading EXIF data.
functions.png_set_sig_bytes: `png_set_sig_bytes` tells libpng how many initial PNG signature bytes you already consumed before calling `png_read_info`. Use it after pre-reading 0–8 bytes from the stream. `num_bytes<0` becomes 0; `>8` is an error; `NULL` `png_ptr` is ignored.
